set.approach: The Cirque of the Towers is entered from the Big Sandy trailhead, following a long trail into the cirque. Scramble up talus and ledges on the far left side of Warrior I, avoiding the slabs directly below the route, then cut back right to the routes when you reach the main upper ledge systems. The route starts on the ledge where the Northeast Face line cuts off to the right, and runs up left-trending ledges to the foot of the evident corner system under a roof.
set.descent_text: Cross the top of the tower to the rappel route that goes down the Northeast Face.

review.notes: Route page: approach and descent; Wolfs Head page: the trailhead for the cirque.

set.approach: The Cirque of the Towers is entered from the Big Sandy trailhead, following a long trail into the cirque. Enter the Warrior I basin, a bit north (left) of the peak, and scramble the grassy ledges rightward until the ground cliffs out; the route starts there, following a ramp system angling up and right.
set.descent_text: Rappel down climber's left of the route.

review.notes: Route page: approach and rappel; trailhead from the cirque page.

set.approach: From the Caves camp, take the main trail toward the Lower Saddle, cross the creek that drains the Teepe Glacier, and take the trail toward the glacier and the guide-service camp. Walk part of the way up toward the glacier, ford the creek a second time and hop boulders to the foot of the tower, which is on your right. The route is on the left of the line called Good over Evil, keeping to the ridge.
set.descent_text: The tower can be descended by rappelling off the top on the side facing the meadows.

review.notes: Tower page: approach; route page: start and rappel. Medium confidence.

set.approach: Drive Highway 16 west from Buffalo, turn right at the Hunter Creek Trailhead sign, take the left fork onto Forest Service Road 391 (rocky; high clearance is recommended) and park at the Enormodome camp, just right of the road at the edge of a large meadow. A faint path leads north from camp to a cattle trail heading northeast; leave it to skirt the boggy meadow on its north side, and a cleared path through the young forest runs straight to the south prow of the dome. The West Face is on the west flank of the fin, and an access staircase in the middle of it gives a third-class scramble to the top. The route is near the centre of the face, left of the staircase.
set.descent_text: Lower off the clip-and-lower anchors at the top.

review.notes: Route page: location and anchors; crag page: access.

set.approach: Approach the cirque from the Big Sandy trailhead and follow the trail along the west side past Pingora into the cirque lake basin. Take the Wolf's Head trail where it splits from the south side of Pingora to a slabby, flowery ramp, and follow it along the base of Wolf's Head, with some fourth-class traversing, to the foot of the route, directly below the thumb-like spire.
set.descent_text: Rappel the route from natural anchors and sling stations. Take care when pulling the ropes, as there are loose blocks and flakes where the rope can stick.

review.notes: Route page: approach and rappel; the crag page notes the descent is time-consuming. Rope length and counts left out.
